chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about two men who were 'hameelayn' (adopted/brothers by contract), who were brought from the land of polytheism. One of them said to the other, 'You are my brother,' and they were recognized by this. Then they were emancipated (freed), and remained acknowledging the brotherhood. Then one of the two died. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The inheritance is for the brother; both are verified.'

key_terms.أَرْضِ الشِّرْكِ: Land of polytheism, referring to the pre-Islamic era or non-Muslim territories
key_terms.حَمِيلَيْنِ: Two men who have established a bond of brotherhood or adoption

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for two men who established a brotherhood bond before Islam and one dies?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the inheritance rights of 'hameelayn' (men who establish a formal brotherhood bond) who were freed from polytheism and remained in their mutual acknowledgment of kinship. The ruling that 'inheritance belongs to the brother' and that their claim is verified (tasdiq) reflects the Shia juristic principle that formalized brotherhood can create legal ties of inheritance, distinct from blood relation, provided the status is publicly recognized and not revoked before death.
